editorial:
Imagine you are on your normal morning commute when a total stranger starts talking to you. That is exactly what happens to Anna when she meets Jesper on the train. At first, it seems like a cute or weird coincidence, but things get creepy fast. Jesper knows things about her that he shouldn't possibly know, like where she hangs out and what she likes. It feels like a lighthearted comedy at the start, but it quickly turns into a wake-up call about how much of our private lives we actually put online for everyone to see.

The acting is great because it makes the awkwardness feel real, and the pacing keeps you guessing. You will probably find yourself checking your own privacy settings while watching this. One downside is that it is a short film, so it ends quickly, but it leaves a strong punch. If you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, go for it, or you could rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. It is a perfect choice for a movie night when you want something short that actually makes you think about your phone habits.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big reveal that Jesper is not a psychic or a stalker in the traditional sense. He simply used all the public information Anna posted on her social media profiles to piece together her entire life. The twist is that Anna willingly gave away all her secrets to the internet. It wraps up by showing how scary it is when a stranger uses your own digital footprint to manipulate you.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tech thrillers and stories about online privacy.
